open_points.subject: A28 clock-read cardinality and ownership
open_points.text: A28 says “one reading per request” and “no second reading”; `system_clock` owns “One wall reading per call” and “one elapsed reading per call”; its Must not own list includes “how many readings it takes”, while each consumer applies the one-instant rule to its own operation.
open_points.question: Is a clock reading shared across the whole HTTP request, taken independently once by each operation or consumer, or taken once by the owning use case with the audit-writer exception; and which module owns any request-wide acquisition and propagation?
options: One wall value is acquired once for the entire HTTP request and passed to authorization, the use case and audit writing.
Each operation calls `system_clock` once independently; one HTTP request may therefore cause several readings, and `audit_writer` takes its own reading.
The owning use case reads once and passes the value to collaborators, except `audit_writer`, which reads separately; authorization is a separate operation with its own reading.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the existing operation rule as controlling: each operation reads once, authorization may read separately, and `audit_writer` takes the stated exceptional reading; replace “per request” with operation-specific language.

witness.initial: An active staff session exists and an expense may be corrected; the wall clock advances during handling.
events: A staff client sends one expense-correction HTTP request.
`authorization_guard` checks the session and current Registry-authorized operation.
`expense_management` writes the corrected expense and its portal-owned timestamps.
outcomes: Reading once for the HTTP request makes authorization, expense timestamps and audit `occurred_at` use one shared instant.

Reading once per operation/call lets authorization and `expense_management` use their own instants and lets `audit_writer` use its stated separate instant, so the expense timestamp and audit `occurred_at` may differ.
witness.observer: An administrator or verification check comparing the persisted expense and its audit record sees the difference.
